new_entities.name: Parent training for ADHD
new_entities.description: Structured parent-focused behavioral training intended to improve child behavior and family management in ADHD.

new_entities.name: Child behavior outcomes
new_entities.description: Child behavior outcomes such as oppositionality, disruptive behavior, and parent-rated functional behavior.

edges.effect_quant: A Cochrane meta-analysis found significant parent-training effects on internalizing behavior in the pooled subset of two studies (n = 142), and later randomized trials also reported improved child externalizing or ADHD-related behavior versus wait-list control or treatment as usual.
edges.population: children with ADHD and their caregivers receiving structured parent-training interventions
edges.mechanism: Training changes how parents cue, reinforce, and respond to child behavior, which can reduce coercive cycles and improve daily behavioral functioning even when core ADHD symptoms persist.
edges.summary: Parent training has a credible behavioral benefit signal in ADHD, especially for disruptive behavior and family-level functioning. It should be framed as a practical behavioral-management intervention rather than a cure for core attentional dysfunction.
edges.caveats: Benefits vary by outcome source and are often stronger for parent-reported behavior than blinded or school-based measures. Some programs improve parenting more consistently than they improve all child behavior domains.

evidence.citation: Zwi M et al 2011 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Parent training interventions for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children aged 5 to 18 years.

evidence.citation: Weinblatt U et al 2021 J Atten Disord
evidence.notes: Parent training in non-violent resistance for children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a controlled outcome study.

evidence.notes: Parent training for preschool ADHD: a randomized controlled trial of specialized and generic programs.
